distinguishing_features: Active variable-stiffness tuned-mass damper mounted on the pipeline span rather than passive monitoring of a bearing/rotor resonance shift.
Feed-forward tuning from recorded flow rate and pressure to a calculated vortex-shedding frequency rather than inference from vibration RMS and operating frequency.
Real-time mechanical detuning/suppression of flow-induced resonance and fatigue rather than early-warning detection of lubricant film thinning.
Piezoelectric stiffness actuator and control logic for adapting damper frequency across variable flow conditions.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce fatigue of a submerged pipeline span subjected to variable flow-induced vortex shedding without adding new sensors or major structural modifications.
parsed.viable_reason: As written, the proposal does not establish that a small piezo-tuned TMD can shift the pipeline span resonance away from shedding across the stated flow range, and its tracking/detuning relations are internally inconsistent.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Given prior art 3's stiffness-frequency resonance teaching and the known TMD relation f proportional to sqrt(k), using existing flow telemetry to compute shedding frequency and retune a damper is a routine feed-forward application.
